body.purpose: Running prose. Verdana, a system face, downloaded for nobody.

data.purpose: Language data only, never interface text. Charis SIL plus the self-hosted Noto script stack; carries IPA and non-Latin scripts the UI face cannot.

shadows.name: lift-popover
shadows.purpose: The hint popover, the only element in the system that floats. Its 1px ink border does most of the separating; the shadow only seats it.

shadows.name: lift-plate
shadows.purpose: The how-it-works screenshots on hover only, never at rest. The rise is what earns the shadow.

motion.name: ink-wipe-out
motion.purpose: The same fill retreating on hover-off.

motion.name: plate-rise
motion.purpose: A screenshot plate lifting 6px on hover. Reduced motion holds it still rather than jumping it.

components.name: Filter Chip

components.name: Data Table
components.description: The signature component. Real table markup inside a horizontally scrolling container, so the page body never scrolls sideways.

narrative.northStar: The Reference Grammar, read on a screen
narrative.overview:
A scholarly linguistics volume that happens to accept typing, moved off paper. The subject is a Warlpiri locative suffix or an Armenian transliteration, and the design's job is to present that subject accurately and then get out of the way. Density is closer to a printed page than to an application: rules are hairlines, corners are square, and chrome yields to legibility.

What chromatic colour there is belongs to NACLO. The site is unofficial and says so, but it is a study tool for one competition, and taking that competition's own two hues rather than inventing a third is the honest move. Both were sampled from naclo.org's stylesheet and logo artwork rather than interpreted from them.

The ground is not theirs. #0d1b2a replaced a flat white that read as a printed page rather than as something you work in, and it is the one part of the palette borrowed from elsewhere. It pays for itself twice: both brand hues clear 4.5:1 against every ground here and so set type at full strength, which they could not do on white, and --surface has somewhere above the ground to go again, so a table reads as an object rather than as a hairline.
keyCharacteristics: A dark navy ground (#0d1b2a) carrying NACLO's own orange and cyan; the hues are theirs, the ground is not
Square corners everywhere; the radius scale exists in tokens and is unused
Hairline rules and tonal blocks carry structure instead of shadows; exactly one element floats
Geometric sans for identity, a system sans for interface, and a dedicated linguistics face for language data
Three colour roles, each with a job: action, correct, and cost/error
A free-text blank grades on Enter and carries no button — three in five questions on the site

rules.name: The Every Colour Has A Job Rule
rules.body: Three chromatic roles and nothing else. Action means action or brand, cyan means correct, oxblood means cost or error. Anything else that needs to stand out does it through weight, rule, or ink fill. A reading-position indicator and a mastery bar are deliberately achromatic: position and progress are neither action nor correctness.

rules.name: The Worst Ground Rule
rules.body: A ratio is solved against whichever ground gives a token the least contrast. On a dark page that is the lightest ground, not the darkest — the ladder runs paper #0d1b2a, surface #152638, tint #1e3449, plus the composites a hovered row makes of tint, and every text token is solved on tint. Opacity counts as a ground: a slash modifier composites the label into the fill beneath it. There is a ceiling too — pure white is 12.78:1 against tint, so a target above that is unreachable rather than hard.

rules.name: The Lifted Surface Rule
rules.body: A raised surface is one tonal step off the ground, and --surface is that step: tables, inputs, popovers, unselected controls. The rule lost its instrument entirely under a white ground, where nothing sits above #ffffff and --surface had to equal --paper. It is whole again. Never write a literal colour for it.

rules.name: The On-Brand-Fill Rule
rules.body: Anything filled with --action carries --on-action and anything filled with --good carries --on-good, never --ink. Both are #000000: 9.88:1 on the orange, 7.98:1 on the cyan. Both brand hues are light, so both take a black label, and --ink is off-white and would fail on either.

rules.name: The Figure Mat Rule
rules.body: Never filter: invert() a problem figure. These are facsimiles of printed booklet pages and at least one problem turns on which monk's robe is white and which is black, so inverting does not dim the figure, it changes the answer. A scan is a white rectangle and on this ground it reads as a hole burned in the page, so a figure is tipped onto its own #ffffff mat with a rule-strong rule, which says the brightness is deliberate. The one sanctioned literal white in the system.

rules.name: The Section Heading Rule
rules.body: NACLO's stylesheet heads every section with an orange h1 over a 1px cyan rule, and .section-head is that. On this ground it is exact: --action-head is #ff9a04 itself, where on white it had to be walked down to clear the large-text floor. Display headings only, 30px and up. The small uppercase labels that head a working surface keep --ink-soft.

rules.name: The Third Voice Rule
rules.body: Language data is set in the data stack, never the UI face. Charis SIL is a linguistics face carrying IPA and extending into Armenian, Devanagari, Georgian, Cherokee, Ethiopic, N'Ko and katakana. A Warlpiri word and the sentence describing it should not look like the same kind of thing.

rules.name: The Sideways Scroll Rule
rules.body: The page body never scrolls horizontally. A wide table scrolls inside its own .table-scroll container, which is why a sticky table header cannot be hung on a th: that container is the scrollport on both axes.

dos: Do keep the page on the navy ground and let --surface do the lifting; a raised thing is a tonal step, not a border alone
Do solve a new colour against the worst ground it can land on, which here is the lightest — --tint and the composites of it, never --paper
Do leave a problem figure's tone alone and keep it on its white mat
Do set every span of language data in the data stack, and add a font subset before shipping a script the fonts do not cover; the build fails on an uncovered character, and that failure is the feature
Do reach for --action-deep or --good-deep when a brand hue sets small text, though on this ground the vivid values clear the floor too
Do give wide tables their natural width inside .table-scroll
Do cap prose by character measure (54ch to 68ch), not by container width
donts: Don't write a literal #ffffff, a literal bg-white, or text-ink on a brand fill; the one exception is the figure mat, which is the white of the printed page and must not follow the ground
Don't remove color-scheme: dark from :root; unset, the browser paints its own scrollbars and form controls light under a dark page
Don't reintroduce a light theme as a class or a second copy of the palette; if a second theme returns it is one list of light-dark() declarations switched by color-scheme
Don't add a fourth colour role; if something needs emphasis and is not an action, a cost, an error, or a correct answer, use weight, rule, or ink fill
Don't introduce a border radius; every corner is 0px and the radius tokens are vestigial
Don't give any control a shadow, or add ambient shadow to a card, panel or table; the hint popover is the only element that carries one
Don't reflow or wrap a data table to fit a narrow screen; column alignment is often the problem itself
Don't put an em dash in user-facing copy, or a character the self-hosted fonts do not carry
